pageCache.pageTitle: The White House School, Poole | Specialist SEND Education
pageCache.text:
The White House difference
The White House difference Small, personal and deeply caring - preparing every child for a positive, independent life
Come on a journey and discover the ‘White House Way’
The White House Way is our whole-school personal development and cultural capital programme, designed to enrich learning beyond the classroom. Through carefully planned experiences, life skills, community opportunities and real-world learning, pupils build confidence, independence and a strong sense of belonging. Alongside our academic curriculum, it is a key part of our Learn & Thrive approach, helping every pupil develop Healthy Minds and Happy Hearts and preparing them for life beyond school.
Pupils access one of two pathways...
Curiosity Pathway
Ages 6-11
Our Curiosity Pathway supports pupils to access the National Curriculum through personalised adaptations, alongside life skills, emotional literacy and independence.
Discovery Pathway
Ages 6-14
Our Discovery Pathway supports pupils with complex needs through a highly personalised, communication-focused and sensory-informed curriculum, building engagement and independence.
Our Learn & Thrive approach helps every pupil become ready to learn and prepared for life, building confidence, independence and belonging.
More about us >
Ofsted Inspection, 2025
Every achievement deserves to shine. Each week, our Star of the Week celebrates a pupil who has shone, grown or achieved something special – successes that make us proud.
From Speech and Language and Occupational Therapy to ELSA, LEGO-Based Therapy and sensory support, our interventions help every pupil thrive.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEN Support | The White House School
pageCache.text:
SEN Support
We offer a specialist learning provision which emphasises the development of core academic understanding, encourages creativity, celebrates outdoor learning and promotes the growth of essential life skills, including mindfulness and emotional literacy. Our academic focus is balanced with consistent and specialist pastoral and therapeutic support, to nurture pupils’ self-esteem, personal, social and emotional development. We are committed to each pupil’s holistic development for them to reach their true academic potential in preparation for their next setting and adult life.
growth
Our Therapeutic Support
Where pupils have identified provision specified in their EHCP, we have a team of Therapy Assistants and work with our Speech and Language Therapists and Occupational Therapist to meet our pupils’ needs and offer a variety of therapies.
Communication & Interaction Interventions
A social development program that uses LEGO activities to support the development of a wide range of social skills within a group setting. Playing with LEGO in a therapy setting promotes social interaction, turn-taking skills, sharing, collaborative problem-solving and the learning of concepts. It can be used to target goals around social skills, language and motor skills.
Our speech and language therapist will assess our pupils and devise a bespoke programme which will be delivered by our Therapy Assistants. Programmes are reviewed regularly by our speech and language therapist.
Self-awareness & self-esteem
Body language & the way we talk
Conversational skill
Making & maintaining friendships
Assertiveness
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Interventions
A proactive, skills-based approach that uses simple, common language to understand, talk about, and teach emotional regulation. Zones of Regulation is integrated into our weekly curriculum and helps pupils to recognize and organise their feelings; states of alertness and energy levels into four coloured zones – blue, green, yellow and red. It is a systematic framework with a developmental sequence of lessons; a consistent, metacognitive pathway to follow for self-regulation.
we have a trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA) to help children develop the skills they need to manage emotions, build relationships, and thrive socially and emotionally. ELSAs are trained and regularly supervised by an Educational Psychologist. Our pupils benefit from ELSA support if they need a little extra help with:
🌈Managing feelings such as anger, sadness, or anxiety
💬 Building confidence and self-esteem
👭 Developing friendships and social skills
🎯 Coping with life changes such as bereavement, family separation, or moving school
🧩 Learning how to solve problems and deal with conflict
A safe and gentle therapeutic approach, which provides an effective way for pupils to process emotional pain or trauma they may be experiencing. This may be through drawing or through sand play. It is a short-term, time limited, pro-active intervention that enables the pupil to express their feelings differently from ordinary verbal language.
an intervention that empowers and inspires pupils to creatively build symbolic models to help them to communicate their thoughts and feelings. The box of specially selected metaphors allows young people to convey their own personal feelings, thoughts, hopes and wishes in a powerful and constructive manner. It can support pupils to build resilience and help them to understand their thoughts, feelings, worries, aspirations, self-regulation and set goals.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Interventions
A sensory integration intervention. It involves a sequence of physical activities that are designed to start with alerting activities, move to an organising phase and then finally to a calming phase. The sensory circuit aims to facilitate sensory processing to help children regulate and organise their senses to achieve the ‘just right’ or optimum level of alertness required for effective learning.
Some children and young people will have bespoke OT programmes designed for them by an Occupational Therapist. This may also include the need to purchase specialist equipment. Our Therapy Assistants will deliver programmes. Programmes can also support emotional regulation and fine and gross motor skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | The White House School, Poole
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
An ambitious, nurturing and personalised curriculum that helps pupils feel safe, build confidence and prepare for life beyond school.
We know our pupils as individuals, including their strengths and their barriers to learning. Our bespoke curriculum and teaching approaches are carefully designed to remove those barriers, making learning accessible, meaningful and successful for every child.
At The White House School, our ambitious, nurturing and highly personalised curriculum is designed to make learning possible again. By removing barriers through adaptive teaching, integrated therapeutic support and meaningful life experiences, we enable every pupil to feel safe, belong, achieve and thrive. Together, we develop the knowledge, confidence, independence and life skills needed for pupils to be Ready to Learn and Prepared for Life.
Ready
Prepared
Our USP evolves around the central focus of supporting our pupils with emotional regulation, to ensure they are ‘ready to learn’. This involves bespoke positive behaviour support strategies as well as regular mindful activities and teaching approaches.
Alongside this, our dedication to our pupils is to ensure that they are ‘prepared for life’, in whatever that looks like for them on an individual basis. For some, it may be in the world of work. For others, it will be most important that they can have sustainable and independent leisure activities and the skills developed to be able to access their local community.
Our curriculum centres around:
Preparation for adulthood
Community inclusion
Independent living skills
Life skills
Emotional Regulation
Communication development

Our Communication Curriculum
Communication is at the heart of learning at The White House School.
Communication
At The White House School, communication is central to everything we do. We recognise that strong communication skills are the foundation for learning, relationships, independence and wellbeing.
Because we know our pupils as individuals, we understand how each child communicates and how they need others to communicate with them. Our bespoke communication curriculum removes barriers to learning by giving pupils the tools, strategies and confidence they need to express themselves and understand the world around them.
Through our Healthy Minds, Happy Hearts ethos and Learn & Thrive curriculum, communication development is embedded across every subject, every classroom and every interaction throughout the school day.
Our Total Communication approach
We use a Total Communication approach, meaning pupils are supported to communicate in whatever way works best for them.
All pupils at The White House School learn Signalong, helping to create a shared communication system across the school community.
It supports pupils to understand spoken language, express themselves clearly, communicate with peers and build confidence in social interaction.

A personalised communication journey
Each pupil has an individual Communication Profile within their Pupil Passport. This helps staff understand how the pupil communicates, how they prefer others to communicate with them, how communication changes depending on regulation level and which strategies support them best.
Speech and language therapy programmes, targeted interventions and daily structured opportunities to practise communication are carefully integrated into each pupil’s learning journey.
Across the Curriculum
Communication is taught explicitly and embedded across all curriculum areas.
Communication is central to English, phonics, reading, writing and mathematics learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Support | The White House School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Support
At The White House School, we have built a blended approach to behaviour, emotional regulation and wellbeing. This helps us personalise support around the needs of each pupil.
Personalised
Support
Pupil support at The White House School is built around consistency, relationships and individual need.
We support pupils through predictable routines, emotionally available adults, low-arousal approaches and close partnership with families and professionals. This helps pupils feel safe, understood and ready to learn.
How we support pupils
Consistent routines and transitions
Clear expectations and boundaries
Reducing sensory overload
Providing advanced warning of changes
SPELL Framework
SPELL stands for Structure, Positive approaches and expectations, Empathy, Low arousal and Links.
Structure
Structure makes the world more predictable, accessible and safer. We use visual information and structured environments to support pupils.
Positive approaches and expectations
We build self-confidence and self-esteem by recognising pupils’ strengths, interests and abilities.
Empathy
We try to understand each pupil’s point of view, including what motivates, interests or worries them.
Low arousal
Calm, ordered approaches and environments help reduce anxiety and support concentration.
Links
Pupils, parents, carers and professionals are seen as partners. Clear communication helps support feel joined up.
‘Every adult is an emotionally available adult’
Emotional regulation isn’t something pupils “just know”, it’s learned and practised with skilled adult support.
By modelling co-regulation and teaching pupils how to manage their feelings, we significantly reduce anxiety and escalation.
“Every interaction is an intervention.”
Relational practice is the foundation of our approach. Adults know pupils well and support them to become the best version of themselves and achieve their potential.
Social skills and friendship
Pupils are supported to develop social skills through weekly social skills sessions, friendship skills work and therapeutic intervention when needed.
Repairing relationships after incidents
We place a strong focus on dignity and trust when supporting pupils through dysregulated times. Every incident is followed by pupil reflection and staff debrief, so we can listen to the voice of the child and use this to inform our practice and provision.
PRICE and trauma-informed practice
The White House School is a PRICE-trained school.
Trauma-informed practice is at the heart of our approach. We believe that all behaviour is communication and, if pupils could do better, they would.
It is our role as adults to be their calm, bring them calm and help them feel safe.
Trauma-informed practice can be seen throughout our positive behaviour support, relationships, use of language, attendance support, classroom environment, adaptive teaching, staff training, self-esteem work and the way we listen to pupil voice.
All staff are trained in the PACE approach: Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy.
We aim to meet the individualised needs of our pupils through excellent teaching and high quality approaches and strategies in every class.
We have a whole school offer for those pupils needing extra support which includes therapies such as ELSA, drawing and talking, groups with lego, think bricks, personalised behaviour support etc.
For those in crisis or needing a more multidisciplinary approach We work closely with all partners such as CAMHS, external safeguarding teams, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, social workers, the Local Authority and external training providers.
Embedding sensory and movement breaks
Using calm, positive and low arousal communication
Safeguarding and pupil wellbeing
Safeguarding sits at the heart of pupil support at The White House School. Our staff work closely with pupils, families and external professionals to help children feel safe, heard and understood.

pageCache.pageTitle: House System | The White House School
pageCache.text:
House System
Helping pupils feel part of a supportive community where everyone belongs, contributes and succeeds together.
At The White House School, our House System helps pupils feel part of a supportive community where everyone belongs, contributes and succeeds together.
Each pupil joins one of our four school houses:
These houses bring pupils together from across different classes and pathways, helping to build friendships, confidence and a strong sense of identity within our school community.
Our House System plays an important role in promoting our core values of Ambition, Resilience and Community, while supporting our whole-school ethos of Healthy Minds, Happy Hearts.
Building a sense of belonging
Being part of a house helps pupils develop a strong connection to the wider school community.
Through house activities, pupils:
This shared experience strengthens relationships across year groups and encourages pupils to feel connected to the whole school.
Leadership within our houses
Each house is supported by a staff Head of House, who helps lead house events and encourages teamwork and participation across the school year.
Pupils are also given opportunities to take on leadership roles as House Captains and Sports Captains, supporting their house teams and helping to organise and promote house activities.
These roles help pupils to:
Leadership opportunities such as these form an important part of The White House Way, supporting pupils to grow in independence and self-belief.
Celebrating effort, achievement and values
House points are awarded throughout the school day to recognise when pupils demonstrate our school values:
Ambition
Trying something new, showing effort and developing independence
Resilience
Persevering through challenges and managing emotions positively
Community
Showing kindness, respect and responsibility towards others
House points help pupils understand that success is about effort, growth and teamwork as well as achievement.
Working together across the school
Pupils take part in a range of house activities across the year, including:
These experiences help pupils develop confidence, teamwork and pride in representing Jupiter, Saturn, Mars or Mercury.
A shared celebration of success
House achievements are celebrated regularly through assemblies and whole-school events, helping pupils recognise their own progress and the successes of others.
Through our House System, pupils learn that they are an important part of something bigger than themselves – a caring community where everyone can learn and thrive with Healthy Minds and Happy Hearts.
The White House Way
Admissions
“Relationships between staff and pupils are very strong. Pupils learn the importance of healthy relationships and form firm friendships.”
Ofsted, 2025
